evidence: Ov. M. 6.9: Phōcaicō bibulās tingēbat mūrice lānās (Lewis & Short: “to soak in color, to dye”)
Hor. C. 2.16.36: lānās … mūrice Afrō (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: First to wet or soak (tunica sanguine Centaurī tīncta, Cic. N.D. 3.70, Lewis & Short), and so to dye; the dye is in the ablative.

sources: Lewis & Short: tingo
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 167, 308.
Quotations marked “Lewis & Short” are given as Lewis & Short cites them, in the house spelling; they have not been checked against a modern edition.
